item.title: Yum China Serves Up the Ingredients for Rerating
item.description: Even unloved stocks deserve another chance when the timing is right. As investors rotate away from artificial intelligence-related bets and back into consumer shares, they should reconsider an overlooked trade: Yum China Holdings Inc., Asia’s largest restaurant group.
item.dc:creator: Juliana Liu

item.description: Attention, Americans: There’s no “right” or “wrong” way to pass the time Tuesday, so long as you voted.

item.title: The RBI Is Key to India’s Bond Market Puzzle
item.description: India is the fastest-growing major economy in the world. A one-time dollar-deposit program for its diaspora has just lifted foreign-exchange reserves by 20%. The rupee is steadying and tax revenues are surging. The bond market should be the darling of investors at a time of geopolitical tension.
item.dc:creator: Srinivasan Sivabalan

item.title: Critical Minerals Face Demand Risks Despite $65 Billion Funding Boom
item.description: In the world of critical minerals, it’s either a drought, or a flood.
item.dc:creator: David Fickling

item.title: AI Investment Boom Demands Stronger Financial Oversight
item.description: The unprecedented investment boom to build out the infrastructure for artificial intelligence is projected to reach more than $10 trillion, if all current plans are realized. The money is coming from many sources, including corporate cash flows, public equity and debt issuance, private debt issuance, off-balance sheet lease obligations and guarantees to AI data center developers from so-called hyperscalers and the leading chip provider, Nividia Corp.
item.dc:creator: Bill Dudley

item.title: The Royal Family Can Afford to Apologize for Slavery
item.description: King Charles III will use his Tuesday speech to the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Antigua and Barbuda to express his “sincere sorrow” over slavery and its brutal legacy. That’s a worthy start, but it’s still not enough. A formal apology is also in order given the British monarchy’s deep, historic involvement in the slave trade and the attendant generational riches it harvested.
item.dc:creator: Rosa Prince

item.title: DOJ Failed Charges Against FBI Officials Show Abuse of Power
item.description: If you were to ask me whether the Justice Department’s failed effort to charge two former FBI officials with lying to Congress about Hunter Biden’s laptop was due more to incompetence or duplicity, my answer would be: Why choose? It could easily be both. In either case, the department’s willingness to sacrifice the liberty of former public servants is a disgrace.
item.dc:creator: Barbara McQuade

item.title: Apple Earnings: Tight-Lipped CEO John Ternus Fails to Inspire
item.description: Apple Inc. investors and fans hoping to get an insight into the philosophy of new Chief Executive Officer John Ternus on Monday were left sorely disappointed. The 51-year-old’s first earnings call was a timid affair, with Ternus taking cover behind a carefully written script as analysts peppered him with questions.
item.dc:creator: Dave Lee

item.title: Insurers Didn’t Learn From the Financial Crisis
item.description: “You might not believe in climate change, but your insurance company does” is a common joke about climate change. Because obviously the companies that pay claims after weather disasters are well aware the planet has grown hotter and more chaotic. Sadly, knowledge isn’t the same thing as wisdom.
item.dc:creator: Mark Gongloff

item.title: The Gold and Bitcoin Slump Reinforces the Dollar's Dominance
item.description: The world remains in a volatile situation: There’s unrest in France over its deteriorating finances, and big political changes are potentially afoot in the US and Israel. Then there’s the ongoing war with Iran, including increased attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and Houthi strikes against Saudi Arabia. item.dc:creator: Jonathan Levin

item.title: London's Oxford Street Has a Message for the UK Economy
item.description: Christmas shopping in London will never be the same. Oxford Street has become permanently vehicle-free along a 1-kilometer stretch, in what the city’s mayor describes as a momentous occasion that puts the UK’s most famous retail thoroughfare on par with New York’s Times Square, the Champs-Elysees in Paris and Barcelona’s La Rambla. Banning traffic offers no magic elixir for the rest of the country’s struggling high streets. There are wider lessons in this historic transformation nonetheless.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Brooker

item.title: Ray-Ban's Family Woes Catch a Czech Billionaire’s Eye
item.description: Delfin Sarl, which controls the €45 billion ($50 billion) estate of the late Italian eyewear magnate Leondardo Del Vecchio, is now caught in a bidding war between a Czech billionaire and one of the eight family heirs to the wealth. Neither proposal is likely to resolve the inheritance squabbles besetting the holding company behind Ray-Ban owner EssilorLuxottica SA.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Felsted

item.description: Traders are listening more when Iran is doing the talking.
